settings.adapt.purpose: When a task cannot go on because something is missing, Branch works out what it is, tells you what would fix it and what that costs, and gets it only after you say yes. Then the task carries on from where it stopped.
settings.advanced.code.intro: Branch can use a language server or a debugger you already have on this computer — the same kind of program a code editor uses to underline mistakes, jump to where something is defined, rename a name everywhere at once, or stop your code on a line. Nothing is ever downloaded, and nothing starts until you switch it on.
settings.advanced.code.keep: Anything Branch starts here stops again when the task that started it is done, so nothing is left running that nobody is watching. Tick these to keep them up between tasks instead, which makes the next task start sooner.
settings.advanced.code.title: Help with code
settings.advanced.diagnostics.help: If you need help with a problem, save a diagnostics folder and pass it on by hand. It holds the health checks, version numbers, a list of what your recent tasks did, and the model prices in use. Your messages, your files and your keys are left out, and you can read every file before you share it.
settings.advanced.promise.lead: Branch sends no usage data to anyone.
settings.advanced.promise.rest: Nothing about you, your tasks or your files leaves this computer unless you send it yourself.
settings.advanced.tools.intro: Your assistant can have far more tools than fit in one message. Each time it works, it carries the few it needs in full, keeps a short list of names for the rest, and looks the others up when a task calls for them.
settings.advanced.tools.title: How the assistant finds its tools
settings.advanced.trace.note: Off unless you turn it on. When it is on, each finished task is written as one file that tracing viewers can open. The files stay on this computer; nothing is sent anywhere.

settings.chat-live.commands-note: /stop, /status, /new, /compact, /usage and /btw. When needed: only /stop, /status and /btw, and only while a task works.
settings.chat-live.intro: Choose what the chat shows and accepts while Branch works on a message. Commands typed in a chat start off; the rest is on.
settings.chat-live.splitting-note: Long replies are split at paragraph breaks and code blocks stay code. When needed: only for replies with code.
settings.chat-live.status-note: Typing, a reaction on your message, and one message that lists the steps. When needed: only once a task has taken a few seconds.
settings.chat-live.steering-note: A message sent while a task works becomes a note it reads next. On also answers quick messages as one. Off: it waits its turn.
settings.chat-permissions.allow-note: Names separated by commas, such as files.write. Commands on this computer, your other devices, your mail, calendar and house, and writing to other chats are never allowed from here.
settings.chat-permissions.approvals-note: Off, and a question about what this line allows is shown in the chat with No only, saying the yes has to be given here in the window. On, and this person on this app can answer yes from the chat, but only to what this same line allows. Name the app and the person for it to do anything: a line written with * for either keeps the tick and no more. Be sure before you turn it on: a chat app cannot prove who is typing, so anyone who gets into that chat account, or who manages to pass themselves off as it, can approve those changes from their own phone. They still cannot say yes to everything from now on, and never to anything this line does not allow.
settings.chat-permissions.channel-note: The name you gave the app in the connections file, or * for every one of them.
settings.chat-permissions.empty: No lines yet: every chat may only read and answer.
settings.chat-permissions.extras-note: Off, the lines below do nothing and every chat gets the short list only. Turning it on lets each line add what it names, for the app and the person it names. Whatever a line adds is still asked about before it happens, and that yes has to be given here in the window — unless you tick the box below for that one line.
settings.chat-permissions.intro: A message in a chat app cannot prove who is typing, so its task may only read and answer: ask you a question, read a file, read what Branch remembers, read a skill you installed, and look something up on the web. Everything else is refused until you allow it here.
settings.chat-permissions.may-answer: may say yes in the chat
settings.chat-permissions.note-note: Your own words, so the line still means something a year from now.
settings.chat-permissions.sender-note: Their id on that app, as it appears under the people who may message you, or * for everybody on it.
settings.deployment.no-safety-copy: No safety copy has been taken yet. One is taken automatically before each update.
settings.dictation.cannot: This computer has no speech program that can write words out as you speak.
settings.dictation.intro: Speak, and the words appear in the message box as you say them, on this computer, for nothing, and nothing is sent anywhere. It uses a streaming speech program you installed yourself — Branch installs none of its own and downloads none — so where this computer has none, the line below says which one to install and the switch stays off. Dictation fills the message box; it does not send it. You press send, exactly as if you had typed. Nothing is written to disk, nothing is kept beyond the phrase being written out, and the words go to the screen rather than into any record. Words appear about a second behind you and may change as it hears more. Dictation is the owner's: nobody else who uses this computer is offered it.
settings.dictation.mode-note: Off, the Dictate control is not there and nothing can open the microphone. When needed, it appears once a conversation is open on screen. On, it is always there. That is the whole difference: which windows offer the control. On does not mean the microphone is open — no setting here ever opens one: only pressing Dictate does, and only at this window. Lockdown switches it off whatever this says.
settings.dictation.open: The microphone is open right now.
settings.dictation.silence-note: Nobody speaking for this long ends the phrase and lets go of the microphone. Branch does not hold a microphone open for a room that has gone quiet.
settings.dictation.warning: Read this before you switch it on: while dictation is listening, the microphone stays open. A recording program runs for as long as you are dictating, which is what lets the words appear as you speak. This is the one place Branch holds a microphone open — the word that starts a turn takes one window of sound at a time and lets go of the microphone every window; this does not. It is opened when you press Dictate and closed the moment you press it again, a quiet room ends the phrase, the conversation closes, Branch is locked, or Lockdown comes on. The line below is on for exactly as long as the microphone is.
settings.file.announced: {name}, {size} kB. Your assistant knows it is there and reads it if the work calls for it.
settings.file.carried: {name}, {size} kB, read at the start of every task.
settings.file.empty: {name} is empty, which is taken to mean there is nothing to say.
settings.file.missing: Not written yet. Make the file and it will be read.
settings.file.no-room: {name}, {size} kB. Switched on, but the others filled the room, so it is named to your assistant instead.
settings.file.not-trusted: Not read: this workspace folder is not trusted. Trust it under Permissions to have it read.
settings.file.off: Not read. Turn it on above.
settings.file.permission-shaped: {count} of these lines ask for permission. Your assistant still reads them, but permission comes from your approval rules and nothing written in a file can change that.
settings.intro.flow-yaml: Writes a saved flow out as YAML text you can keep or send, and reads a flow back from YAML as a new flow. Building on Branch must be switched on.
settings.intro.health: Checks the pieces this app depends on and tells you what to do if one is not right.
settings.intro.keychain: Branch reads a password only for an entry listed here, and only when a task needs it. This list holds names, never passwords.
settings.intro.make-this-workspace-feel-: Make this workspace feel like yours.
settings.intro.screen-switch: Off to start with. When needed, the screen tools are fetched only when a task calls for them; on, they come with every task.
settings.intro.sdk-kit: Lets another program you write use Branch: gives an AI coding tool the list of web routes and working code for each language, and lets flows be written out and read back as files.
settings.intro.speech-engines: Write speech out or read replies aloud with Deepgram, ElevenLabs, Azure, or a program on this computer such as Piper. Keys stay in Secrets; you only name them here.
settings.intro.system-voice: Off to start with. Reads replies aloud with the voices already on this computer, free and offline.
settings.intro.video-programs: Uses ffmpeg and yt-dlp, if they are already on this computer, to look at still pictures from a video, write out what is said in it, and save videos or their captions from the web. Branch never installs them.
settings.intro.what-this-computer-allows: This computer has switches of its own. Branch never changes them; here is what each one is for.
settings.learning-core.confirm: Forget everything Branch has learned from experience? This cannot be undone.
settings.learning-core.draft-opened: A draft skill from the steps that kept working is open below. Read it, change it, and install it if you want it.
settings.learning-core.empty: Nothing learned yet. Turn it on and work as usual; habits appear here after a few tasks.
settings.learning-core.forgotten: Forgotten. It starts again from nothing.
settings.learning-core.kept: It keeps what it learned about {count} tools, skills and notes, on this computer only.
settings.learning-core.saved: Saved. It applies from your next task.
settings.local.purpose: Run a model here instead of in the cloud: nothing leaves this computer and nothing is charged. Branch checks what your computer can handle and suggests a size that will feel right.
settings.local.routing-note: Off by default. When it is on, Branch still does exactly what you choose for a conversation.
settings.lockdown.intro: The one switch that refuses commands and makes everything else wait for your yes.
settings.lockdown.note: Refuses, without asking, running a command or a script, using your screen and keyboard, borrowing your browser and your other devices. Every other tool waits for your yes. Turning it off puts back exactly the settings that were there before.
settings.note.agents-file: A file in the project folder saying how you want work done here. Written after something goes the wrong way, it changes the next task rather than the one after you remember to mention it.
settings.note.files-cannot-grant: A file can change how your assistant works and how it talks to you. It cannot give it permission it does not already have — your approval rules decide that, every time a tool runs.
settings.note.heartbeat-file: A list your assistant reads each time it wakes on a schedule. An empty file means there is nothing to do and it goes back to sleep without spending anything.
settings.note.learning-core: Branch notices which tools, skills and notes helped in tasks like yours, and which did not. It asks no model to do this and keeps no words from your requests.
settings.note.learning-core-forget: Forgetting clears only what this has learned. Your notes, skills and conversations stay as they are.
settings.note.learning-core-modes: Off: nothing is learned. When needed: it learns, and your assistant asks it when the work calls for it. On: it also chooses what to try first at the start of every task.
settings.note.memory-file: Everything else here your assistant remembered on its own. This is a file you write, so you can open it, read the whole thing and change your mind about any of it.
settings.note.persona-files: Write these in plain words and your assistant reads them before it does anything else. What you put in the first one replaces its built-in character rather than being added to it.
settings.note.security-audit-mode: Off: only when you press the button. When needed: your assistant can also run the check when you ask it whether your setup is safe. On: it also runs each time Branch starts.
settings.note.security-check: Looks over how Branch is set up on this computer — who else can read its files, who can reach it, and what it may do without asking — and puts right what it can.
settings.note.security-fix: Fixing only ever takes other people’s access away from Branch’s own files. Everything else needs a decision from you, so it is described instead.

settings.second-opinion.debate-intro: For a question worth the cost, two connections answer on their own and then read each other. It stops at whichever of these two it reaches first, and says which one stopped it.
settings.second-opinion.intro: Have another connection read a finished answer and say whether it stands up. It is shown beside the answer and never written into it, so you read both. Off until you turn it on, and it costs what any other model call costs.
settings.second-opinion.same-connection-: Leaving this on the one that answered is a weaker check: a model rarely argues with itself.

settings.voice.liveViewNote: On: pressing Talk live, or the send button while the message box is empty, opens a calm view with a circle that moves with the sound, what each of you says as it is said, Mute and End. The microphone is asked for the first time you press it, never before. Off: Talk live is the plain button it always was.
settings.wake-word.cannot: This computer cannot listen for a word.
settings.wake-word.intro: Say your own word and Branch starts a turn, instead of holding the Talk button. Listening happens on this computer only: no sound ever leaves it, no file is written, and nothing is recorded or kept before your word has been heard — one window of sound is held, asked about, and dropped. Not every computer can listen: the line below says what this one really does, and whether it is listening this moment. While the switch is off, nothing listens at all and the microphone is let go of. Holding Talk stays the ordinary way in, and the word gives nothing away — the turn it starts is asked about exactly as the same words typed into the box would be, with the same questions. It carries only the one window your word was in, a second or two: nothing said after that window is heard, because no further sound is recorded. On Windows the engine listens for that one phrase alone, so there the turn carries just your word and nothing else.
settings.wake-word.listening: Listening for your word right now.
settings.wake-word.mode-note: Off, nothing listens. On, it listens whenever Branch is running. When needed is not wired up yet — nothing tells the listener whether a conversation is open on the screen, so it says so rather than listening all the time. Lockdown switches it off whatever this says.
settings.wake-word.sureness-note: Out of a hundred. Lower hears your word more often, and more often hears it when you did not say it.
settings.wake-word.word-note: Two or three syllables work best, and something you would not say by accident. With no word chosen there is nothing to listen for, so nothing listens.

updates.channel.note: Stable installs published releases, each checked against its fingerprint before it is installed. Beta builds every merged change on this computer, the moment it lands, before the full checks: it needs git and Node.js, each update takes a few minutes, a copy of your data folder is kept first, and with “update by itself” on it installs each change as soon as no task is working. Stable remains the default. Switching back never installs an older version.

updates.source: Updates come from the Branch Agent releases on GitHub. Each download is checked against its published fingerprint before anything changes.

vault-autofill.hint.address: Optional. Branch will not fill a page that pressing something took it to on another website, because what it pressed was put there by whoever wrote the page — unless the address is this one, written here by you.
vault-autofill.hint.also: Optional. Other exact website names this same sign-in may be filled on, one per line, such as accounts.example.com. Branch never works one out for itself: if signing in happens on a different name from the one above, write that name here.
vault-autofill.hint.code: Tick this when the same item holds your authenticator code. Branch then types the code the same way, and sees it no more than it sees the password.
vault-autofill.hint.item: The item's name, exactly as it appears in your password manager. Branch never guesses which item to use from what a page says.
vault-autofill.hint.name: The name you will ask for, in lower-case letters, digits and dashes, such as shop.
vault-autofill.hint.remove: Takes this sign-in off the list. Nothing in your password manager is changed.
vault-autofill.hint.service: Which password manager holds it. Branch reads it only from a password manager you set up under “Where Branch reads saved sign-ins from” above, and can only read. A one-time code is read from Bitwarden only.
vault-autofill.hint.site: Just the website name, such as example.com. Branch fills this sign-in on that exact website and nowhere else — not on a name under it, such as pages.example.com, because a name under a website can belong to somebody else.
vault-autofill.hint.switch: Off, Branch refuses and the assistant is not offered the tool at all. When needed, and On, it fills one of the sign-ins below when you ask for it by name. It is yours alone: a message from a chat app, a short-lived key, another computer, someone else on this computer and a Trunk are all refused, and so is everything while Lockdown is on.
vault-autofill.intro: Branch can type a password you already keep in your password manager straight into a page you are on, when you ask it to by name. It never shows you or the assistant the password, keeps no copy of its own, and only ever fills a page on the exact website you saved the sign-in for. While a recording of the browser is being kept, it fills nothing at all.

window.flows.tour.apps-text: Each with its real recipe: make the bot, paste what it gives you, Branch checks it, you approve a six-digit code, save.
window.flows.tour.asks-text: Anything that sends, deletes, spends or installs waits for your yes: Send it, Always allow, or Don’t. The Inbox collects them all.
window.flows.tour.board-text: Work that takes more than one sitting. Trunks move their own cards; drag one to move it yourself.
window.flows.tour.contacts-text: Each Trunk is an assistant with one job. Message it like a teammate. A moving ring means it’s working; a dot means it needs you.
window.flows.tour.find-text: Ctrl K opens every conversation, place, setting and command.
window.flows.tour.gateway-text: Keeps your Trunks running when Branch is closed, and starts Branch again if it ever stops.
window.flows.tour.in-person-text: Each Trunk can have a character. It acts out what the Trunk is really doing: thinking, searching, reading, working, waiting for you, celebrating, resting. Change it in the Trunk’s Look tab.
window.flows.tour.label: Tour
window.flows.tour.layout-text: Ctrl B hides the list. Drag any edge: narrow the list to icons, widen the side panel, or give the computer more room. Double-click an edge to reset.
window.flows.tour.left-text: The ring shows the account used next. Click it for every plan’s 5-hour, daily and weekly limits.
window.flows.tour.local-text: Branch looks at your memory and graphics card and only offers what fits. One click installs it; it runs free and private.
window.flows.tour.may-do-text: Auto, Ask first, Plan first or Full access, per conversation. Shift+Tab switches; Lockdown stops everything.
window.flows.tour.media: Sound and video in the chat
window.flows.tour.media-text: Recordings play where they were sent. Hover any message to pin it, so it stays in front of the assistant however long the conversation runs.
window.flows.tour.memory-text: The ring shows how full memory is. Tidy up finds facts said twice, facts that disagree, and ones nobody uses.
window.flows.tour.model-text: The model and how long it thinks. The choices change with the model.
window.flows.tour.pane-text: Activity, Plan, Files and Memory beside the conversation. Drag its edge to any width; double-click to reset. The browser and computer open full size instead.
window.flows.tour.pets-text: Pick one of dozens of pets to walk along the list, and a painted scene to sit behind the glass. They nap, cheer and follow what your Trunks are doing.
window.flows.tour.places-text: Overview at a glance, Inbox for what needs you, Automations for work on its own, Library for what it remembers and made, Team for everyone who uses Branch, Customize for Trunks, skills and chat apps.
window.flows.tour.plus-text: Attach files, @mention a Trunk, use a skill, go Temporary, have it ask questions first, or choose who answers.
window.flows.tour.self-text: Ask it to change its own settings or gateway. It tries the change on a throwaway copy, shows you before and after, and every change can be rolled back.
window.flows.tour.settings-text: Regular, Advanced or Technical: just the essentials, or every file, port and raw key.
window.flows.tour.team-text: Who’s here and what their Trunks are running right now, shared Trunks, teams of Trunks, usage and rules.

window.switch-on.stayed-off: It is still switched off. Lockdown keeps some features off until it is turned off.
window.switch-on.tidy-where: Tidy my memory runs from Library › Memory, Tidy up. Its report is different every time, so it stays a proposal here.
window.switch-on.triggers-why: A trigger is kept as a procedure that starts after one of your tasks finishes, so these must be on before you can confirm one.
window.themes.copied: Copied. Paste it on another computer (Themes › Paste a theme code) or send it to a friend.
window.themes.not-a-code: That isn’t a Branch theme code. It starts with {"branchTheme":1.
window.updates.card.gentle: It builds at low priority so your computer stays quick, which can make it take a few minutes.
window.updates.card.installs-by-itself: Installs by itself when nothing is running.
window.updates.card.paused-task: Holding back while a task works. It carries on when the task is done.
window.updates.card.paused-typing: Holding back while you type. It carries on a few seconds after you stop.
window.updates.paused.task: holding back while a task works
window.updates.screen.restarting: Branch closes and opens again by itself.
window.updates.why.build: The new version didn’t build, so nothing changed.
window.updates.why.check: The new version didn’t pass its check, so nothing changed.
window.updates.why.copy: The safety copy couldn’t be made, so nothing changed.
window.updates.why.download: The new version couldn’t be downloaded, so nothing changed.
window.updates.why.fetch: The new version couldn’t be fetched, so nothing changed.

window.what.fill-required: Fill in each field before preparing the draft.
window.what.lede: Everything Branch can do for you right now. Try it starts a new conversation with the request ready for you to send.

window.what.title: What can Branch do
window.why.a-container-per-trunk: Branch has no container per Trunk: a container is picked per approval rule, and only when Docker is already on this computer.
window.why.aa-low: Branch already works this way: an account is used once the ones above it in the order run out. Put it Last to keep it for then.
window.why.ac-fall: No model runs on this computer yet. Set one up under On this computer first.
window.why.ac-next: There's nothing to move between yet: add a second account to a connection first.
window.why.ad-crash: Branch has nowhere to send crash reports to yet.
window.why.adaptgob17: Stays off here until a separate safety review: a yes installs a program and starts the task again.
window.why.adaptpickb17: Stays off here until a separate safety review: a yes installs a program and starts the task again.
window.why.agent-perm: Stays off here until a separate safety review: choosing what it may be asked changes your approval rules.
window.why.archive-facts-unused-for: Branch never archives a fact on its own: tidying memory suggests setting aside facts untouched for 180 days, and each one waits for your yes.
window.why.b-new: This follows your approval mode, not a switch of its own: the careful mode asks once for each new site. Permissions › “Use the browser on this computer” sets what the browser may do without asking.
window.why.b-watch: Branch has no setting for this; the browser view opens only when you open it yourself.
window.why.bg-new-off: Switch on The shared commands in Settings › General to start one with /bg.
window.why.call17d: Branch can't make phone calls; its Twilio connection only sends and receives text messages.
window.why.chaintamperb17: It would have to draw made-up entries. A real break shows as Link broken on its own entry.
window.why.chfmt17d: Branch writes each chat app's own style; choosing another isn't in Branch yet.
window.why.chw-may: Stays off here until a separate safety review: who may use Branch from this chat app.
window.why.chw-who: Branch answers each chat app itself. A Trunk answers there only in a chat that carries on its conversation, and only if Customize › Trunks lets it reach that app.
window.why.chx17d: These are set for every chat app at once, under Settings › Chat apps › What the Trunk sees and Staying connected.
window.why.cloudnew17d: Computers in the cloud need a keepoak.com account, which isn't open yet.
window.why.cmsw17d-call: Branch can't make phone calls; its Twilio connection only sends and receives text messages.
window.why.cmsw17d-meet: Branch has no bot that joins Meet, Teams or Zoom. With your Microsoft account connected, a Trunk can summarise a Teams meeting's transcript afterwards.
window.why.comp-remote: Stays off here until a separate safety review: a computer reached over SSH gives Trunks another machine to work on.
window.why.comp-sandbox: Branch can't make a private computer on this PC yet.
window.why.d17-devpick: Stays off here until a separate safety review: it lends a phone's camera or location.
window.why.d17-examples-go: Stays off here until a separate safety review: copying an example installs its code on this computer.
window.why.d17-handoffcli: Only Branch itself hands a coding job to your own Claude Code or Codex; a Trunk can't.
window.why.d17-harness: Branch doesn't look for other assistants' skill folders on this computer. A skill written as a SKILL.md can be added with Add a skill.
window.why.d17-hookaddr: Stays off here until a separate safety review: each address carries its chat app's secret word.
window.why.d17-hooks-go: Branch runs each hook only when its event happens; there's no way to run them by hand.
window.why.d17-leads-go: The desktop app doesn't save downloads from the window; open Branch in a browser to export the list.
window.why.d17-lint: Branch checks a skill's name and description when it's added, and refuses one that fails; there's no check to run again on the skills you have.
window.why.d17-locker: The engine doesn't say where its locker lives, so there's nothing true to show yet. Your keys are listed by name under Settings › Secrets, and their values never come back out.
window.why.d17-pages-go: An article needs a topic, and this list has no place to type one. Ask for one in a conversation.
window.why.d17-tokens: No engine check reads your sign-ins' tokens yet, so there's nothing to run. The tokens stay encrypted in the locker and are never shown in the window.
window.why.d17-turnhook-go: Stays off here until a separate safety review: turning a hook on lets a program run on this computer after every answer.
window.why.d17-voiceapprove: The window has no Answer aloud beside a waiting question yet, so there's nothing to try here. When it comes, a spoken yes answers one question only, for two minutes, and a risky one still needs a press to confirm.
window.why.d17-watches-go: A watch needs the page or search to watch, and this list has no place to type one. Ask a Trunk to watch it.
window.why.docedit17: An exact edit is made by a Trunk from your request in a conversation; this dialog has no place to say what to change. Compare shows what differs.
window.why.downloads-may-come-from: There's no switch for this: Branch's browser downloads only from the sites its launch settings file lists, and keeps only the file types on its download list.
window.why.f15-a-local-index-of-mail-cal: Branch keeps no local index: it searches your mailbox and calendars on their own servers each time you ask.
window.why.f15-add-sign-ins-from-outside: Bringing sign-ins in from your everyday browser would hand tasks in the sandbox every site you're signed in to, and Branch has no way to do it. Sign in inside the sandboxed browser instead, one site at a time.
window.why.f15-ai-and-ai-comments-start-: A comment in a file would start a task as you, so anyone who can write to a watched folder, such as a cloned project or a synced folder, could start one. It runs only from the terminal, where you name the folder each time: branch watch <folder> --ai-comments.
window.why.f15-always-read-in-full: Branch pins a skill to one conversation at a time, not to every conversation, so there's nothing to choose for all of them here.
window.why.f15-check-install-requests-fo: Stays off here until a separate safety review.
window.why.f15-code-map: Always on, not a setting: a Trunk can ask for a ranked map of the project's files whenever it works on code.
window.why.f15-deep-research-reports: Deep research has no switch of its own in Branch.
window.why.f15-edit-documents-exactly: Exact document edits have no switch of their own in Branch.
window.why.f15-filter-long-lists-before-: Branch doesn't filter what a Trunk reads with a decision model yet: a line it dropped would be hidden from the Trunk, with no way to get it back.
window.why.f15-follow-up-tasks: A Trunk leaves itself a task as a card on the Board, which has its own switch in Automations; there's no separate one here.
window.why.f15-hold-back-keys-found-in-a: Always on: a key found in an answer is blanked. There's no switch, so the guard can't be weakened.
window.why.f15-its-own-settings: Stays off here until a separate safety review: Branch changing its own settings.
window.why.f15-join-from-your-calendar: Branch has no meeting bot, so it never joins a meeting from your calendar.
window.why.f15-keep-team-conversations: Teams need a keepoak.com account, which isn't open yet.
window.why.f15-keep-versions-of-what-tru: Always on: each time a file is kept under the same name it becomes a new version with its checksum, up to 20. There's no switch.
window.why.f15-listening: Set these one at a time: the push-to-talk key and the wake word each have their own row below.
window.why.f15-load-tools-only-when-need: Always on: each round Branch loads only the tools it needs and keeps the rest a search away. There's no switch.
window.why.f15-loosening-what-it-may-do: Always asks: Branch never loosens what it may do without your yes.
window.why.f15-mix-models-on-hard-questi: Turn on Pick the model per task first, with two different connections picked under Defaults: a hard question is asked of both.
window.why.f15-number-the-clickable-thin: Always on, not a setting: whenever a Trunk uses the browser it can number what's on the page and press things by number.
window.why.f15-only-signed-skill-package: Stays off here until a separate safety review.
window.why.f15-password-manager: Windows Credential Manager is part of Windows, and this Branch runs on another system, so it can't read from it here.
window.why.f15-pick-the-model-per-task: Choose both first under Defaults: Quick and cheap jobs, and Planning and hard problems.
window.why.f15-pin-ssh-hosts: Always on, not a setting: Branch reaches a computer over SSH only if its key is already in your known_hosts, and stops if that key changes.
window.why.f15-portable-mode: Portable mode is a file named portable.txt beside the program, read when Branch starts, so it can't be switched from here.
window.why.f15-practice-runs: Practice runs are only the /dry-run command in the terminal, one conversation at a time.
window.why.f15-procedures-that-start-the: These run their steps without asking you each time, so they're switched on in Automations, where Branch asks you to confirm first.
window.why.f15-projects-pick-up-matching: Branch can name the project a request belongs to, but never moves a message there by itself; switching projects is always your step.
window.why.f15-push-to-your-phone-and-br: Branch has no push of its own to phones or browsers. ntfy or Pushover can reach your phone as a chat app, added in the connections file.
window.why.f15-record-browser-tasks: No switch: a Trunk keeps a browser recording when it starts one in a task. To record every task, use Permissions › “Record tasks so you can watch them again”.
window.why.f15-recording: Branch can't make phone calls, so there's no call to record.
window.why.f15-relay-for-chat-app-accoun: Stays off here until a separate safety review: a relay brings chat messages in from another machine, paired with a secret.
window.why.f15-restarting-its-own-engine: Stays off here until a separate safety review: Branch restarting itself.
window.why.f15-run-the-browser-in-a-sand: Stays off here until a separate safety review: it moves the browser into Docker or onto a Playwright server you run.
window.why.f15-save-task-trajectories: Nothing to switch on: Branch already keeps each task's record. Ask in a conversation to export a task, or run runs.export from the Playground.
window.why.f15-search-documents-by-meani: Always on when your model service can compare meaning: documents are searched by meaning as well as by words. There's no switch.
window.why.f15-send-notes-afterwards: Branch has no meeting bot, so there are no meeting notes to send.
window.why.f15-share-memory-between-trun: Each Trunk keeps its own memory and also reads the facts you mark as shared, but never writes into them. Branch sets this for each Trunk, not for all at once.
window.why.f15-spending-that-needs-an-ad: Teams need a keepoak.com account, which isn't open yet.
window.why.f15-status-line-script: Branch builds the status line from its own pieces and runs no script of yours for it. Pick Default or Minimal.
window.why.f15-tables-and-charts-from-sp: Tables from spreadsheets have no switch of their own in Branch.
window.why.f15-the-gateway-s-timings: Stays off here until a separate safety review: this is a standing rule in what Branch may do.
window.why.f15-tool-scripts-and-webassem: Stays off here until a separate safety review: these run code Branch was handed, even inside a sealed box.
window.why.f15-tools-that-join-over-a-we: Stays off here until a separate safety review: a program that joins lends Branch tools it didn't have.
window.why.f15-use-what-the-trigger-sent: Always on: every trigger's prompt can use {{payload}} and {{field.path}}. There's no switch.
window.why.f15-verify-each-release: Always on, not a setting: every update the desktop app downloads must match its published SHA-256 checksum, and a build provenance record when GitHub has one, before it installs.
window.why.f15-which-browser: Stays off here until a separate safety review: borrowing your own Chrome lets a Trunk use your signed-in sites.
window.why.f15-who-it-may-call: Branch can't make phone calls, so there's no list of who it may call.
window.why.file-app: Branch has no way to open a file in its own app from here.
window.why.file-edit: Branch has no way to edit this file from here yet.
window.why.fl-send-set17c: Branch has no way to send a flag to the Branch team; each flag stays on this computer.
window.why.fl-send17c: Flags are kept on this computer only. Branch has no way to send one to the Branch team.
window.why.from-now-on-for-a-specialist: Stays off here until a separate safety review: a standing instruction changes every later task. Say “From now on …” in a conversation instead; Branch asks you once before keeping it.
window.why.g-all: Stays off here until a separate safety review: it would answer requests without naming each one. Answer each with its own Yes or No.
window.why.gate-script: Stays off here until a separate safety review: Allow lets this program run on this computer before every turn. Until then the job stays paused, so Cancel would change nothing.
window.why.group18c: Branch has no groups yet, so there's nothing to make. What each person here may use is set on their card in Settings › People.
window.why.grp-talk: Always on in a room: its Trunks talk it through, up to 3 rounds, and any Trunk can pass. There's no switch for one room.
window.why.gw-tray: Only the desktop app has a tray icon, and it always shows one; there's no setting for it.
window.why.hoaccept18b: Stays off here until a separate safety review: who may take over a team's task.
window.why.hops: This is how Branch works, not a setting: a chain of Trunks messaging each other stops after three hops, and one task sends at most three messages.
window.why.horeject18b: Stays off here until a separate safety review: who may take over a team's task.
window.why.if-write: Stays off here until a separate safety review: it runs a tool by hand.
window.why.img-bg: Branch can't set a picture from a conversation as the background yet.
window.why.img-save: Branch already keeps every picture it makes in Library › Made for you; it has no saving of its own.
window.why.install: Set this in Notifications › Check for updates: Install when idle.
window.why.keep-warm-no-claude: Only a Claude connection with an API key is kept warm, and none is set up.
window.why.knobs-owner-only: Only the owner changes these. Switch back to the owner's profile to change them.
window.why.knows: Branch keeps no list per Trunk: while Trunks messaging each other is on, any of your Trunks may message any other.
window.why.ko-start: keepoak.com accounts aren't open yet, so there's nothing to connect.
window.why.lane18b: A member's conversation opens only as a view-only page that leads back to the room, which isn't in this window yet; as an ordinary chat it would start work outside the room.
window.why.loopstartb17: A stopped loop starts again only from /loop in its own conversation.
window.why.m-effort-none: The model in use doesn't take a thinking effort.
window.why.m-img: The connection that answers now can't make pictures (a ChatGPT sign-in or a Claude connection can't). Make an OpenAI-compatible or Gemini model the one that answers, then choose its picture model here.
window.why.m-openrouter-only: Set up an OpenRouter connection first: the list of companies comes from OpenRouter itself.
window.why.m-vid-svc-off: Turn on Make short videos first; the service is chosen while it is on.
window.why.machine: Branch starts single tasks on another computer, but can't hold a conversation there yet.
window.why.machine-keepoak: keepoak.com accounts aren't open yet, so there's nothing to connect.
window.why.mcp-test: Stays off here until a separate safety review: trying a server starts the program you typed.
window.why.meet17d: Branch has no bot that joins Meet, Teams or Zoom. With your Microsoft account connected, a Trunk can summarise a Teams meeting's transcript afterwards.
window.why.mkteam18c: A team takes one to eight specialists, and there are none yet.
window.why.nbtryb17: It would break the running engine on purpose, so it isn't offered here.
window.why.ob-brain-model: This model has no accounts to switch. Choose which model answers in Settings › Models.
window.why.ob-mail: Signing in to Google or Microsoft isn't in this window yet.
window.why.ob-restore: Stays off here until a separate safety review: a backup brings back settings and rules as well as your conversations. In a terminal, branch restore <file> does it now.
window.why.obt-signin: Signing in to Google or Microsoft isn't in this window yet.
window.why.p-install: Installing has no approval kind of its own: an add-on, skill or plugin is changing settings, and a package a command installs is running a command. This shows on only when both go without asking.
window.why.p-inv-keepoak: Teams need a keepoak.com account, which isn't open yet.
window.why.p-wall: This computer can't build that wall; the reason is written under this row.
window.why.phone-access-needs-pin: Set an App lock PIN first. Your phone asks for it every time it takes a task's browser.
window.why.phone-access-no-door: The Mini App's page isn't open on this computer right now. Restart Branch, then try again.
window.why.plug-add: Stays off here until a separate safety review: a plugin is code that runs on this computer. One you put in Branch's plugins folder shows here.
window.why.pp-may: What each person may do comes from their role. Change their role on their card to change it.
window.why.pp-own: Always on: each person's conversations and records are their own. There is no way to share them yet.
window.why.pp-pin: Always on: switching to a person always asks for their PIN. To be asked for yours when switching back to you, turn on Ask for my PIN in Team › Signing in.
window.why.prompt-try: Asking two models at once is the Model arena's, which spends on two connections and ships off. Save the prompt, then ask it under Settings › Models › Model arena.
window.why.quit: Close this tab to leave. Branch itself keeps running, so your Trunks keep working.
window.why.reload-without-dropping-work: Branch has no reload apart from a restart. Restart the engine stops it with work saved; with Carry on interrupted work by itself on, tasks pick up again.
window.why.restart16: Restarting from the browser window needs the desktop app, or use Branch itself › Restart the engine.
window.why.revoff17d: Branch can turn Telegram off only by deleting its saved token. Paste the new token instead.
window.why.rewrite-short-notes: The window has no note picker for this. Ask in a conversation: Branch rewrites one of its notes clearer, shorter, fixed, as a list or more formal, as a suggestion.
window.why.rninstall17d: Installing goes through the desktop app's own updater. Turn on “Keep Branch up to date by itself” under Settings › Updates & about.
window.why.rule-up8: Stays off here until a separate safety review: moving an Allow above a Never would loosen your rules, and Branch has no way to move one rule yet.
window.why.run-join: Asking to join needs a keepoak.com team, and keepoak.com accounts aren't open yet.
window.why.scope: A pick here is for this conversation only. What every new conversation starts on is set in Set up Branch › How much it asks.
window.why.self-dev: Stays off here until a separate safety review: Branch working on its own code.
window.why.self-dev-remote: Working on its own code needs Branch to send Git work to GitHub. Switch that on under Integrations first.
window.why.selfdo15: A yes means writing the terms Branch's own source is prepared under, and the window has no place to write them yet; publishing has no route of its own.
window.why.session-key: Branch keeps one session key for as long as it runs and can't swap it while running, and a new one would sign out every window and phone paired with this computer. For a key that ends by itself, use branch token create in the terminal.
window.why.share-a-trunk: Sending a Trunk out through Git or as a skill bundle would publish its instructions and what it remembers, and Branch has no step yet that shows you what leaves before it goes. To save a Trunk as a file you can check first, use Share this Trunk… in its conversation menu.
window.why.share-handoff: Branch can't hand a conversation to a chat app, the terminal or another agent yet.
window.why.share18c: Branch can't share a conversation with another person yet: on this computer each person's conversations are kept apart, and nothing here opens one to someone else.
window.why.shot: The message box can't take a picture of your screen yet; attach a picture you took instead.
window.why.si-lock: Always on, not a setting: after five wrong PINs a profile locks for five minutes, so the guard can't be weakened.
window.why.stage-step: Branch keeps no picture of the screen for each step, so an earlier step can't be shown.
window.why.sugg15-reg: Stays off here until a separate safety review: Add downloads this skill from the registry's address.
window.why.sys16-browser: Only the desktop app opens this computer's own settings. In a browser, open them yourself and find this permission there.
window.why.tool-log: No route shows a server's own output; why it didn't start is shown above.
window.why.tool-perm: Stays off here until a separate safety review: choosing what a tool may do changes your approval rules.
window.why.tool-retry-launch: This server comes from your launch file, and Branch has no way to start it again from here.
window.why.tool-rm-kept: This one is in your launch file or your plugins folder, not in Branch's own list, so remove it there.
window.why.tool-test: Stays off here until a separate safety review: a test starts the server's program without asking you first.
window.why.tool-upd: Only skills added from a registry have newer versions Branch can look for; servers, programs and plugins don't.
window.why.tool-who: Stays off here until a separate safety review: choosing which Trunks may use it widens or narrows what they can reach.
window.why.tool9g-launch: This server is switched on and off in your launch file, not here.
window.why.tr-models: Teams need a keepoak.com account, which isn't open yet.
window.why.tr-skills: Teams need a keepoak.com account, which isn't open yet.
window.why.tr-sso: Teams need a keepoak.com account, which isn't open yet.
window.why.trig-who: A procedure has no place for a Trunk, so Branch itself does the work.
window.why.undo-the-last-update: The window has no button for this yet. To go back to the version before the last update, run `branch rollback` in a terminal on this computer: it says first whether going back would lose work, and `branch rollback --yes` does it.
window.why.update-remind: Only the desktop app reminds you about a ready update, so in a browser there is nothing to put off.
window.why.vaultwinb17: Windows Credential Manager is part of Windows, and this Branch runs on another system, so it can't read from it here.
window.why.wbwhere17d: Branch learns an app only in its own sealed browser; it has no private computer for this.
window.why.web-search: Branch takes the search service from its launch settings file (web › search) and uses DuckDuckGo until that file names another; the window can't change it.
window.why.when-tools-are-loaded: Branch decides which tools to load every round by itself; there's no setting.
window.why.who-room: The room's own rule answers by @mention, by its lead, or with everyone; it has no "whoever fits" and no member you pick. Its Room rules set it.
window.why.widget6: The snippet would put a key to this computer inside a web page, and anyone who opens that page could read it and use Branch as you. It stays off until a snippet can carry a key that answers only for that page.
window.why.win-min: A browser tab can't minimise its own window; use your browser's own button.
window.why.ws: keepoak.com teams aren't open yet, so Personal is the only workspace.
wsedit.card.note: Open and change text files in your workspace from the Files tab of a conversation. Every save can be put back, and a file that changed since you opened it is never overwritten.
